======================================================================
7. THREE SEPARATE COMPLETENESS CONCEPTS
======================================================================

Mechanically separate:

1. SEMANTIC_TERMINAL_COMPLETE
   The semantic Provider response has reached a valid terminal state.

2. TERMINAL_CAPTURE_COMPLETE
   All bytes/events required to prove the terminal semantic result were durably captured.

3. TRANSPORT_TAIL_CLOSED_CLEANLY
   The underlying transport closed cleanly after terminal.

If current schema can represent these with existing fields, reuse it.
Do not invent parallel state unnecessarily.

Required invariants:

- post-terminal timeout/cancel must not downgrade an already complete semantic result/capture;
- pre-terminal timeout/cancel remains failure;
- Provider error already observed remains primary even if tail timeout occurs;
- ping after terminal may be diagnostic/ignored only if source-grounded.

Create:
shared-completeness-contract-v1.json

constraint_traceability.original_requirement:
======================================================================
8. CAUSAL PRECEDENCE CONTRACT
======================================================================

Define explicit narrow precedence.

Examples:

A. Provider error -> ping -> timeout
PRIMARY = Provider error
TAIL = ping + timeout diagnostics

B. message_stop complete -> ping -> timeout
PRIMARY = successful semantic terminal
TAIL = ping + timeout diagnostics

C. message_stop complete -> cancellation
PRIMARY = successful semantic terminal
TAIL = cancellation diagnostic

D. timeout before terminal
PRIMARY = timeout/transport failure

E. cancellation before terminal
PRIMARY = cancellation/transport failure

F. message_stop -> Provider error
Must follow source-grounded policy and must NOT silently ignore the Provider error.

Do not generalize "first exception always wins" outside this stream boundary.

Produce:
shared-stream-causal-precedence-contract-v1.json
